author: Brooke Park
title: S.F. Tesla driver who fatally struck man crossing highway said car was in full-self-driving mode - NewsBreak
text:
By Brooke Park ,
12 hours ago The California Highway Patrol said a man who was trying to cross a Bay Area highway early Thursday was fatally struck by a person driving a Tesla in full-self-driving mode. (California Highway Patrol) A Tesla driver told officials he was using the car’s full self-driving mode when he fatally struck a 71-year-old man crossing a Solano County highway early Thursday morning, California Highway Patrol said.
The crash occurred around 2:30 a.m. on Interstate 80 westbound at the Interstate 780 interchange, where the Tesla’s dash camera showed the 71-year-old man entering the freeway from the right shoulder while the car was traveling around 70 mph, according to the California Highway Patrol.
The Tesla braked and veered to the left as the man walked into the car’s path but was unable to avoid crashing the right front portion of the car into the pedestrian, the CHP said.
Authorities said that at least one more vehicle struck the man while lying on the highway. First responders arrived and determined the man had sustained fatal injuries. The Solano County Coroner's Office identified the man as Domingo Gonzales. His family could not be immediately reached for comment.
The 26-year-old Tesla driver from San Francisco stopped and cooperated with police, providing the dashcam footage, the CHP said. “The driver stated the vehicle was being operated in Full Self-Driving (FSD) autonomous mode at the time of the crash,” the agency said in a statement.
No other drivers stopped.
The Tesla driver was not cited after the crash, but if the investigation determines the driver was negligent in a way that caused the collision, charges could be filed through the district attorney’s office, CHP officer Scott Heitman said.
Thursday’s fatal crash was the second this month involving a Tesla using full self-driving mode on a Solano County freeway. On Oct. 13, CHP officers were responding to a fatal crash on eastbound Interstate 80 near Fairfield when a Tesla driver crashed into a CHP patrol vehicle, injuring the two officers inside. The Tesla driver, a 22-year-old Sacramento man, told investigators that he was asleep while the car was in full self-driving mode, Heitman said.
Three CHP patrol vehicles had their emergency lights on and four lanes of traffic were closed when the Tesla drove though safety cones and struck the CHP Dodge Charger. CHP did not ticket the man after the crash, officials said.
Tesla’s Full Self-Driving feature can steer, change lanes and park, but it requires drivers to remain alert and supervise the vehicle. Tesla says its 360-degree cameras and other safety features can reduce the severity of crashes or prevent them altogether.
Drivers using the feature must watch the road and be ready to take control. Yet some motorists have admitted to eating or napping while the system was engaged, testing the safeguards designed to prevent distracted driving.
The California Highway Patrol was investigating the crash Thursday and asked anyone who witnessed it or has information on any other vehicles involved to contact the Solano Area CHP office.
